markingScheme.criterion: Quotes the actual numerator/denominator values of one genuine Grid Builder trial from their own Investigation Record (both factors and the resulting product).
markingScheme.accept: Any genuine trial from the student's own record, with both factors and the product stated.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim with no actual fraction values quoted from their own trials.

markingScheme.criterion: States the general rule correctly: multiplying two fractions that are both less than 1 always gives a product smaller than either fraction, because you are taking only 'a fraction of a fraction' of the whole.
markingScheme.accept: Equivalent correct phrasing, e.g. 'you are finding a part of a part'.

markingScheme.criterion: Links this rule to the area-model grid specifically: the shaded overlap is always a smaller region than either the full row-strip or the full column-strip, because it is the intersection of both shaded fractions.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating the numeric rule correctly with no reference to the grid/overlap model.

markingScheme.criterion: (a) Correctly writes the multiplication expression 2/3 x 3/4 (order does not matter) to represent 2/3 of the 3/4 cup of butter.
markingScheme.insufficient: Writing an addition, division, or an expression using the wrong numbers.

markingScheme.criterion: (b) Correctly calculates 2/3 x 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2 cup (or an equivalent correct fraction/decimal), showing working (multiplying numerators and denominators).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct working that arrives at an equivalent value to 1/2 cup (e.g. 0.5 cup).
markingScheme.insufficient: An arithmetic slip in the multiplication, or no working shown alongside a correct-looking answer.

markingScheme.criterion: (c) Explains why 1/2 cup is less than 3/4 cup using their own Grid Builder evidence — e.g. because the shaded overlap region in their own grid trial was smaller than either full strip, since you are only taking a fraction (2/3) of the original 3/4 cup.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general statement that 'multiplying fractions makes them smaller' with no reference to the student's own grid evidence.

levels.descriptor: Achieves 0 of the 3 points above: no genuine grid trial figures are quoted, no general 'product smaller than either factor' rule is stated, and no link is made to the area-model overlap.

Achieves 1 of the 3 points above — most commonly quotes a real Grid Builder trial (both factors and product) but does not state the general rule correctly and/or does not link it to the overlap model.
Achieves 2 of the 3 points above — e.g. quotes a genuine trial and states the general rule correctly, but does not clearly link the rule to the shaded-overlap idea in the grid model.

Achieves all 3 of the points above: quotes a genuine Grid Builder trial from their own record, states the general 'product smaller than either factor' rule correctly, and links it to the shaded-overlap area-model reasoning.

levels.descriptor: Achieves 0 of the 3 points above: the expression in (a) is wrong, the calculation in (b) is wrong or missing, and (c) gives no grid-based explanation.

Achieves 1 of the 3 points above — most commonly writes the correct multiplication expression in (a), but does not correctly calculate the product in (b) and/or does not explain (c) using grid evidence.
Achieves 2 of the 3 points above — e.g. writes the correct expression in (a) and correctly calculates 1/2 cup in (b), but does not also explain (c) with reference to their own Grid Builder evidence.

Achieves all 3 of the points above: writes the correct multiplication expression in (a), correctly calculates the exact amount in (b) with working shown, and explains in (c) why the result is smaller using their own grid evidence.

markingInstructions: This is a Primary 2 student. Mark ONLY the two constructed responses, using each question's point-by-point marking_scheme in marking_context (award each point independently unless it names a dependsOn point, in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded) and each point's accept/insufficient wording. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points (one per lettered part a/b/c) — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity, never overlapping with the content marks. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Accept valid alternative wording or equivalent fractions/decimals; do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 14 (6 auto + 3 + 3 + 2). Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
